summary: Iteration 13 end-to-end verification of Order Confirmation Chat, post-purchase claim-account, /my-orders dashboard, 3s chat polling and 10s notification bell + support-reply email. New backend suite /app/backend/tests/test_claim_chat_v5.py: 14/14 passed (session lookup, guest chat, admin reply, claim-order happy path + security, notifications, order scoping). Regressions: backend_test.py 88/89 (1 flaky), test_coupons_v2.py 21/21, test_coming_soon_v3.py 14/14 serial, test_auth_playbook_v2.py 9/11 (both failures = known ingress-IP lockout keying). Browser: /payment/success for a PAID session shows 'Payment confirmed' + Track Order + order-chat + claim-account-card with read-only pre-filled checkout email; guest posted a message (sender_role customer) and an admin reply posted out-of-band appeared in ~1-2s with NO reload; claim flow created the account, logged in, redirected to /my-orders where the order row, open-chat toggle (3 msg history) and details link all work; notification bell badge appeared ~1s after an admin reply, panel showed 'New message from support' and cleared to 0 on open; guest /my-orders reads localStorage orders and can post; order-detail chat and Admin console chat work both directions; /dashboard renders my-orders-page; nav-my-orders + mobile-nav-my-orders present. Guest support-reply email confirmed delivered (202 Accepted to delivered@resend.dev); fake addresses return the expected 422 'undeliverable recipient'. All test data created was deleted.

minor.issue: Order adoption query is case-sensitive: it lowercases order.user_email then matches {user_email: <lower>}. Any order stored with mixed-case email (only /orders/checkout lowercases today) creates the account but returns orders_claimed=0, silently orphaning the order the buyer just claimed. Use a case-insensitive match or normalise user_email on write.

Brute-force lockout is keyed on '<client.host>:<email>'; behind the ingress the client IP rotates, so lockout fired on attempt 9 (playbook expects 5 fails) and a successful login only clears the counter for the current IP (test_auth_playbook_v2 TestBruteForceLockout x2 fail). Key on email only or trust X-Forwarded-For.
Still no retry/backoff; support-reply/tracking sends fail silently on provider 422/429 with only an ERROR log (pre-existing, carried from iteration 12).

integration_issues.issue: Both components swallow fetch errors in empty catch blocks with no loading/error state. A 403/500 renders the misleading 'No messages yet. Ask us anything about this order.' — seen briefly right after the claim redirect before the next 3s poll succeeded. Add an error state (e.g. 'Could not load messages, retrying…').

MyOrders only renders statuses in ['pending','processing','awaiting_payment'] (Active) and ['completed','cancelled'] (History). Any other/future status silently disappears from the page — add an 'Other' bucket or render the remainder.

action_items: Make claim-order's order adoption email match case-insensitive (or lowercase user_email at write time) so orders_claimed can never be 0 for the order being claimed.
Re-key the login lockout on email (or X-Forwarded-For) so 5 failures actually lock, per the auth playbook.
Add visible error/loading state to OrderChat (and NotificationBell) instead of silently showing 'No messages yet' when the fetch fails.
Render orders whose status is outside the two hardcoded buckets on /my-orders.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py claim_order: {'user_email': email} exact match after .lower() — case sensitivity bug described above; also consider wrapping user insert + orders update in error handling so a failed update_many does not leave an account with zero linked orders.

MyOrders guest branch fires an unbounded Promise.all over every id in localStorage 'pokeforge_guest_orders'; cap it (e.g. last 20) and drop ids that 403/404 so a claimed-then-logged-out device does not spam the API.
PaymentSuccess.jsx makes a separate GET /orders/{id} just for the email; the session endpoint could return the email and save a round trip.
post_message sends the support email inline in the request path (await send_email) — a slow provider directly slows the admin's reply; move to a background task.
server.py is 1067 lines; the messaging/notification and auth sections are natural split points.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Do NOT put the cleanup script in a pytest fixture — pytest.ini runs 2 xdist workers and a per-worker teardown deletes the other worker's live orders (this produced 5 false failures before I moved cleanup out). Run 'python3 /app/scripts/cleanup_test_data.py' after the suite instead. Also: httpOnly auth cookies leak between requests when using a shared requests.Session, which makes 'anonymous' assertions fail (looks like a 403->200 bug but is not) — test_claim_chat_v5.py uses a cookie-less Anon client for this reason. Seed paid orders with /app/scripts/seed_test_order.py [email] (lowercase emails only, see the claim case-sensitivity bug). test_coming_soon_v3.py must be run with -n 0; its checkout-guard test races with the class that toggles coming_soon flags. Known flaky: backend_test.py::TestCouponExclusions::test_product_id_exclusion (~1 in 2 full runs under xdist, passes isolated).
rca_of_the_issue: No functional defect found in the iteration-13 feature set. The claim-order orders_claimed=0 case I hit was reproduced with a mixed-case order email: claim_order lowercases order['user_email'] and then queries orders with that lowercased string, so mixed-case docs never match. Real checkout lowercases the email (server.py line 518) so production flows are unaffected, but the code path is fragile. The two auth-playbook lockout failures reproduce serially and stem from keying login_attempts on the ingress client IP, which rotates across proxy pods.
